editorial:
Imagine a guy who has everything but does absolutely nothing with his life. That is Tom Collier. He is a rich playboy who spends his nights at parties until he meets Christie Sage, a spunky photographer. She pushes him to actually do something meaningful, leading him to run a magazine that fights against everything his snobby family believes in. You get a great mix of romantic sparks and lighthearted comedy as Tom tries to change his ways for the woman he loves. It feels like a classic old-school romance where the chemistry between the leads carries the whole story.

What really works here is the drama that kicks in when Christie rejects Tom's proposal because she feels she does not fit in with his wealthy world. It is heartbreaking but believable. The pacing is steady, though the introduction of the gold-digger Cecelia adds a nice layer of frustration that makes you root for the main couple even more. If you enjoy vintage films with a lot of heart, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: After a miserable marriage to the greedy Cecelia, Tom finally finds a way out. He realizes that wealth and social status mean nothing without true love. In the final scenes, Tom and Christie set aside their past mistakes and misunderstandings. They reunite and decide to commit to each other for real this time. The movie ends on a happy note, showing that love wins over money and social class.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic black and white romances and stories about class differences.
